roman.name: Roman Empire
descriptions: Lasted about 500 years, from 27 BC to 476 AD
Spanned 5 million km² across three continents
Inventor of the Julian calendar, concrete and aqueducts
Built 80,000 km of paved roads connecting Rome to the entire empire
Collapsed in 476 after the barbarian invasions

persian.name: Achaemenid Persian Empire
descriptions: Founded by Cyrus the Great around 550 BC
First empire to use royal roads with a postal service
Stretched from India to Egypt, with 50 million inhabitants
Defeated by Alexander the Great in 330 BC
Left behind Persepolis, a palace-city with carved staircases

macedonian.name: Macedonian Empire
descriptions: Created by Alexander the Great in just 13 years
Largest empire of Antiquity in the 4th century BC
Alexander never lost a battle in his entire life
Stretched from Greece all the way to India
Split into several kingdoms after Alexander's death in 323 BC

egyptian.name: Ancient Egypt
descriptions: Civilization that lasted over 3,000 years along the Nile
Built the Pyramids of Giza, 4,500 years old
Invented hieroglyphs, a writing system with over 700 signs
Pharaohs were considered living gods
Cleopatra was the last queen, in 30 BC

assyrian.name: Assyrian Empire
descriptions: Mesopotamian empire at its peak around 700 BC
First to use iron to arm a large army
Its Library of Nineveh contained 30,000 clay tablets
Its kings were feared for their military campaigns
Disappeared in 612 BC with the fall of Nineveh

babylonian.name: Babylonian Empire
descriptions: Famous for the Hanging Gardens, one of the 7 wonders of the world
King Hammurabi wrote one of the first codes of law
Built the Ishtar Gate, covered in blue bricks
Center of astronomy: divided the day into 24 hours
Destroyed by the Persians in 539 BC

greek.name: Ancient Greece
descriptions: Birthplace of democracy, invented in Athens in 508 BC
Organized the first Olympic Games in 776 BC
Home of philosophers like Socrates, Plato and Aristotle
Built the Parthenon, a temple dedicated to the goddess Athena
Invented theater, with tragedies and comedies

carthaginian.name: Carthaginian Empire
descriptions: Founded around 814 BC by Phoenician sailors
Major maritime power of the western Mediterranean
Hannibal crossed the Alps with 37 elephants in 218 BC
Fought Rome through the 3 Punic Wars
Carthage was razed by the Romans in 146 BC

han.name: Han Dynasty
descriptions: Ruled China for 400 years, from 206 BC to 220 AD
Gave its name to China's majority ethnic group, the Han
Developed the Silk Road linking China to Rome
Invented paper, the compass and the seismograph
Had 60 million inhabitants at its peak

maurya.name: Maurya Empire
descriptions: First empire to unify almost all of India, around 320 BC
Emperor Ashoka converted to Buddhism after a great battle
Built engraved stone pillars across all of India
Had an army of 600,000 soldiers and 9,000 elephants
Promoted the spread of Buddhism across Asia

byzantine.name: Byzantine Empire
descriptions: Continuation of the Eastern Roman Empire, from 395 to 1453
Constantinople was Europe's largest city for centuries
Emperor Justinian built the Hagia Sophia basilica
Spoke Greek and practiced Orthodox Christianity
Fell after the capture of Constantinople by the Ottomans in 1453

mongol.name: Mongol Empire
descriptions: Largest contiguous empire in history, 33 million km²
Founded by Genghis Khan in the early 13th century
Its cavalry could cover 100 km per day
Stretched from Korea all the way to Central Europe
Promoted exchange between Asia and Europe via the Silk Road

carolingian.name: Carolingian Empire
descriptions: Founded by Charlemagne, crowned emperor in 800
United France, Germany and northern Italy
Charlemagne revived schools and culture in Europe
Aachen housed his palace and his famous chapel
The empire split into three in 843 with the Treaty of Verdun

holy-roman.name: Holy Roman Empire
descriptions: Existed for 1,000 years, from 962 to 1806
Brought together hundreds of small German states
The emperor was elected by seven prince-electors
Voltaire said it was neither holy, nor Roman, nor an empire
Dissolved by Napoleon in 1806

abbasid.name: Abbasid Caliphate
descriptions: Great Muslim caliphate founded in 750
Baghdad was the world center of knowledge in the 9th century
Its House of Wisdom translated Greek and Indian texts
Developed algebra, the algorithm and Arabic numerals
Destroyed by the Mongols in 1258 with the capture of Baghdad

mughal.name: Mughal Empire
descriptions: Ruled India from 1526 to 1857
Emperor Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal in memory of his wife
Produced some of the finest miniatures and jewels of the East
United Hindus and Muslims under one crown
Once owned the Koh-i-Noor diamond, now in London

khmer.name: Khmer Empire
descriptions: Dominated Southeast Asia between the 9th and 15th centuries
Built Angkor Wat, the largest religious monument in the world
Its capital Angkor had up to 1 million inhabitants
Mastered irrigation with huge reservoirs called baray
The empire declined after the capture of Angkor in 1431

mali.name: Mali Empire
descriptions: Great African empire between the 13th and 15th centuries
Emperor Mansa Musa was the richest man in history
Controlled gold and salt across the Sahara
Timbuktu was a major center of Islamic studies
Stretched across present-day Mali, Senegal and Guinea

aztec.name: Aztec Empire
descriptions: Dominated central Mexico from 1428 to 1521
Tenochtitlan was built on a lake, with floating gardens
Cocoa was used as currency for shopping
Spoke Nahuatl, a language still alive in Mexico
Conquered by the Spaniard Hernán Cortés in 1521

inca.name: Inca Empire
descriptions: Largest pre-Columbian empire, along the Andes mountain range
Built 40,000 km of paved roads through the mountains
Builders of Machu Picchu, lost city at 2,400 m altitude
Used neither the wheel nor writing, but knotted quipus
Conquered by the Spaniard Francisco Pizarro in 1533

ottoman.name: Ottoman Empire
descriptions: Lasted over 600 years, from 1299 to 1922
Captured Constantinople in 1453, ending the Byzantine Empire
Suleiman the Magnificent built the Blue Mosque of Istanbul
Covered three continents: Europe, Asia, Africa
The empire disappeared after the First World War

british.name: British Empire
descriptions: Largest empire in history by area, 35 million km²
It was said the sun never set on it
Dominated a quarter of the world's population in the 19th century
Left English as a global language
Main decolonization between 1947 and the 1960s

french-colonial.name: French Colonial Empire
descriptions: Second largest colonial empire after the British
Had territories in Africa, Asia and the Americas
Algeria was considered part of France
Left French as an official language in 29 countries
Decolonization between 1945 and 1962, ending with the Algerian War

spanish.name: Spanish Empire
descriptions: First global colonial empire, starting in 1492
Dominated South America, Central America and the Philippines
Introduced potatoes and tomatoes to Europe
Spanish is spoken by over 500 million people today
The Empire lost its last colonies in 1898

portuguese.name: Portuguese Empire
descriptions: Oldest European colonial empire, created in 1415
Lasted nearly 600 years, until 1999 with the return of Macau
Vasco da Gama opened the sea route to India in 1498
Colonized Brazil, Angola, Mozambique and Goa
Portuguese is spoken today by 280 million people

russian.name: Russian Empire
descriptions: Empire founded by Peter the Great in 1721
Third largest empire in history, after the British and Mongol
Stretched from Poland all the way to Alaska
Catherine II made Russia a great European power
Ended with the Russian Revolution of 1917

austrian.name: Austro-Hungarian Empire
descriptions: Empire with two capitals, Vienna and Budapest, from 1867 to 1918
Ruled by the Habsburg family for 700 years
Had 11 nationalities and just as many languages
Home of Mozart, Freud and Empress Sissi
Dismantled after the First World War

german.name: German Empire
descriptions: Created in 1871 by Bismarck by unifying the German states
The emperor bore the title of Kaiser
Leading industrial power in Europe at the end of the 19th century
Triggered the First World War in 1914
Disappeared in 1918 with the abdication of Kaiser Wilhelm II

japanese.name: Empire of Japan
descriptions: Modern empire formed in 1868 with the Meiji era
Modernized Japan in just a few decades
Dominated East Asia during the first half of the 20th century
Emperor Hirohito reigned for 63 years
The empire ended with the Second World War in 1945
